title: ee, ea
goal: Read and spell the long-e vowel team spelled **ee** and **ea**.
review: ai, ay, open-syllable long e (he, we, me)

spell.sentence: I need to eat a snack.

listen.passage: Communities that organize regular street clean-ups tend to build a stronger sense of civic pride, because neighbors who work side by side start to feel a shared responsibility for the place they live.

tier2.def: a duty or job that is yours to take care of.
tier2.full: a duty or job that is yours to take care of.

questions: Why might a clean-up build civic pride?
What responsibility do you take seriously?

A.text: Sam and his team go to the beach. / When they see a green kite, they find a sweet, clean spot to sit. / "Let's eat lunch by the sea," said Sam. / They read a page and laugh at a funny bit. / A queen bee comes to see the sweet leaf, then goes home. / Sam and his team feel very happy after a fine day.

B.text: Each week, Kate and her team clean the street by the shop. / When they meet at nine, each one has a task. / Kate likes to see the street stay neat when they are done. / "We laugh a lot, but we get the job done," said Kate. / At the end, the team sits and has a sweet snack, glad for a job well done.
